remediation.suggestion: No security fix is required. If possible, tune marketplace static analysis to distinguish Markdown inline code from executable source code.

content.value_statement: WiFi teams need fast visibility into network health, client quality, and access point load. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through UniFi WiFi analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists WiFi networks and reviews their configuration status.
Checks SSID broadcast information across the UniFi deployment.
Reviews connected WiFi clients and connection status.
Analyzes client signal strength and band distribution.
Checks access point performance metrics for load and coverage issues.
Produces WiFi optimization recommendations based on observed metrics.
limitations: Requires UniFi network tools that provide WiFi, client, and device metrics.
Does not change network settings by itself.
Recommendations depend on the accuracy of available UniFi telemetry.
Does not replace professional RF surveys for complex sites.

use_cases.title: Daily WiFi Health Review
use_cases.description: Review networks, SSID broadcasts, connected clients, and access point status before users report issues.

use_cases.title: Client Connectivity Triage
use_cases.description: Find clients with weak signal, poor band placement, or repeated connection problems.

use_cases.title: Capacity Planning
use_cases.description: Compare client distribution and access point load before adding hardware or changing coverage plans.

prompt_templates.title: Show WiFi Overview
prompt_templates.prompt: Show all WiFi networks, SSID broadcasts, connected clients, and access point status. Highlight anything that needs attention.

prompt_templates.title: Find Weak Clients
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify WiFi clients with poor signal strength or unstable connections. Group them by network, access point, and band.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Band Balance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze 2.4GHz and 5GHz client distribution. Recommend band steering, access point, or coverage changes that could improve performance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit WiFi Capacity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review WiFi networks, broadcasts, clients, signal quality, and access point metrics. Produce a prioritized capacity and optimization plan.

output_examples.input: Show all WiFi networks and their status.
output_examples.output: A concise network summary with each SSID, broadcast status, security notes, connected client counts, and access points that need review.

output_examples.input: Which clients have poor signal strength?
output_examples.output: A ranked list of affected clients with signal quality, current band, likely cause, and recommended next action.

output_examples.input: Compare WiFi performance across all access points.
output_examples.output: An access point comparison covering client load, band distribution, signal quality, and suggested balancing changes.

best_practices: Review signal strength, band placement, and access point load together before changing settings.
Compare current results with known site layout and user location data.
Validate recommendations during low-risk maintenance windows when changes are required.
anti_patterns: Do not treat one weak client as proof of a network-wide outage.
Do not change channels or band settings without checking access point load first.
Do not ignore security settings while focusing only on speed metrics.

faq.question: What UniFi data does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses available WiFi network, SSID broadcast, client, client statistics, and access point performance data.

faq.question: Can it change WiFi settings?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes analysis and recommendations, but it does not directly modify network configuration.

faq.question: Does it help with poor coverage?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify weak signal patterns and overloaded access points that may explain coverage problems.

faq.question: Can it compare 2.4GHz and 5GHz usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for reviewing band distribution and suggesting balancing improvements.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for an RF survey?
faq.answer: No. It supports operational troubleshooting, but complex physical sites may still need a professional RF survey.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
